scope.definition: Any being other than the player characters.
scope.rule: Monster listings describe an average specimen; the Judge may alter any creature's abilities and power level.
Assume all monsters except humans and demi-humans have infravision 60'.

characteristic.name: percent_in_lair
characteristic.definition: Percentage chance that an encounter occurs in the monster's lair.
characteristic.rule: Monsters encountered in their lair are usually present in greater numbers.
Monsters encountered in their lair may have treasure appropriate to their type.

characteristic.name: dungeon_encounter
characteristic.definition: Typical encounter pattern in a dungeon.
characteristic.rule: Use the first collective noun and number for encounters outside the lair.
Use the second collective noun and number for encounters inside the lair.
The in-lair number may be a direct quantity such as 2d6 or a larger organizational unit defined elsewhere, such as 1 warband.
If only one collective noun and one range are listed, the monster does not make a lair.
If the entry is none, the monster is not normally encountered in that setting unless placed there by the Judge for a special reason.
Collective nouns have no game mechanical effect other than referencing encounter quantity.
Number encountered counts only standard combatant creatures.
Chiefs, bodyguards, juveniles, elderly, and sometimes females do not count in number encountered unless a specific description states otherwise.
The monster description defines additional encounter members where relevant.
The Judge is the final arbiter when encounter composition is unclear.

characteristic.name: wilderness_encounter
characteristic.definition: Typical encounter pattern in the wilderness.
characteristic.rule: Read wilderness encounter entries the same way as dungeon encounter entries.
Wilderness lairs are usually the same size as dungeon lairs.
Wilderness lairs can be much larger than dungeon lairs.
Large wilderness lairs are common for human, demi-human, and humanoid encounters.
A large wilderness lair can effectively be an entire dungeon.

characteristic.name: alignment
characteristic.definition: Monster alignment is Lawful, Neutral, or Chaotic.
characteristic.rule: Many unintelligent or alignment-indifferent monsters are Neutral.

characteristic.name: movement
characteristic.definition: Movement is listed as exploration movement in feet per turn and combat movement in feet per round.
characteristic.rule: The value in parentheses is combat movement.
If more than one movement rate is listed, the additional rate is a different movement mode appropriate to the creature, such as flying or swimming.

characteristic.name: armor_class
characteristic.definition: Monster AC functions the same as character AC.
characteristic.rule: Monster AC may reflect agility, natural armor, or magical adjustment.

characteristic.name: hit_dice
characteristic.definition: Hit Dice are roughly analogous to character level, but determine hit points as a number of d8s.
characteristic.rule: A monster with X HD normally has Xd8 hit points.
A printed plus or minus value modifies rolled hit points.
A monster always has at least 1 hp.
Hit Dice determine monster attack throws.
Hit Dice help determine experience points awarded for defeating the monster.

asterisk_rule.definition: Each asterisk next to Hit Dice indicates one special ability for XP purposes.

qualifying_abilities.ability: spell-like abilities or other abilities of similar potency

asterisk_rule.rule: These special abilities increase XP earned for defeating the monster.

dungeon_level_stocking.rule: 1 HD or less monsters are typically found on dungeon level 1.
2-3 HD monsters are typically found on dungeon level 2.
4-5 HD monsters are typically found on dungeon level 3.
6-7 HD monsters are typically found on dungeon level 4.
8-9 HD monsters are typically found on dungeon level 5.
10 HD or more monsters are typically found on dungeon level 6 or deeper.
When monsters are placed on an atypical dungeon level, their Number Encountered should be adjusted accordingly.

characteristic.name: attacks
characteristic.definition: Lists the number of attacks available each round and the nature of those attacks.
characteristic.rule: Attack entries are ordered to match the damage listing.
General special attack rules apply whenever a monster is noted to possess that special attack, unless the monster description states otherwise.

special_attack.name: acid
special_attack.rule: Acid damages on a successful hit by making contact with flesh.
After contact is made, acid continues to deal damage in later rounds without additional attack throws unless noted otherwise.
Most acid can be removed with water or another non-flammable liquid.
special_attack.exception: Black dragon acid breath does not persist round to round; damage is suffered only per attack.
special_attack.rule: If acid destroys armor, adjust the victim's AC as though unarmored.

special_attack.name: charge
special_attack.rule: Any monster may charge using the normal movement rules.
Monsters with natural weapons suited for charging deal double damage on a successful charge.

special_attack.name: charm
special_attack.rule: Monster charm differs from charm person.
The target receives a saving throw versus Spells.
On a failed save, the target becomes confused and passive.
A charmed target cannot use spells or magic items.
A charmed target cannot make decisions.
A charmed target does not defend against the monster's attacks.
If the monster and target cannot communicate, the target still acts in the monster's interest and protects it, even against allies.
Charm effects have a duration.
If the monster is killed, the charm effect ends immediately.

special_attack.name: continuing_damage
special_attack.definition: Some attacks continue to deal damage after the initial successful hit without requiring new attack throws.
special_attack.rule: The monster description states when the continuing damage ends.
Ending conditions usually include the monster's death.

special_attack.name: dive
special_attack.rule: Only flying monsters with talons can make dive attacks.
Targets must be in open terrain for a dive attack to be possible.
A successful dive attack deals double damage.
If both talon attacks hit, the monster may grab the target.
The target must be smaller than the monster to be grabbed.
The target can avoid being grabbed with a successful saving throw versus Paralysis.
If the monster is much larger than the target, the Judge may impose a save penalty of -4, -6, -8, or greater.
Some monsters are large enough to grab with no saving throw allowed.
Once grabbed, the target takes automatic damage each round without further attack throws until escape.
Grabbed creatures are helpless until they escape.
Escape requires a successful saving throw versus Paralysis.
Grabbed creatures may be carried off.
A carried creature falls if it escapes, if the monster releases it, or if the monster is killed.

special_attack.name: energy_drain
special_attack.rule: Energy drain removes class levels from characters and Hit Dice from monsters.
No saving throw is allowed.
The effect can be reversed only by ritual magic such as wish.
When a character loses a level, set experience points to the minimum for the new lower level.
All class-dependent abilities adjust to the new lower level, including hit points and saving throws.

special_attack.name: magic_resistance
special_attack.definition: Magic resistance is a chance to ignore spells and spell-like effects.

procedure.step: When the creature is affected by a spell or qualifying spell-like effect, roll 1d20.
If the roll is equal to or greater than the creature's listed MR value, the creature ignores the effect.

special_attack.rule: The listed MR value assumes a 7th level caster.
Apply a -1 penalty to the resistance target for each caster level above 7.
Apply a +1 bonus to the resistance target for each caster level below 7.
For MR, spell-like effects are effects that duplicate spells or are resisted with a saving throw versus Spells or Staffs and Wands.
Effects resisted with Poison and Death, Blast and Breath, or Paralysis or Petrification do not count as spell-like effects for MR unless they also duplicate a spell.

special_attack.name: paralysis
special_attack.rule: A paralyzed character collapses and cannot move, speak, or cast spells.
The character remains conscious and aware.
A saving throw versus Paralysis avoids the effect.
Paralyzed characters require no attack throw to be hit.
Any unengaged character can slay a paralyzed character in one round with any weapon.
Most monster paralysis lasts 2d4 turns.
Cure light wounds can negate monster paralysis, but heals no hit points when used this way.

special_attack.name: petrifying_gaze
special_attack.rule: Meeting the gaze requires a saving throw versus Petrification or the victim turns to stone.
Surprised opponents automatically meet the gaze.
Opponents attacking without averting their eyes or using a mirror also meet the gaze.
Fighting while averting the eyes imposes -4 on attack rolls and -2 AC.
Fighting via mirror reflection is safe from direct gaze.
Using a mirror imposes -2 to attack and no AC penalty.
A petrifying-gaze monster is not immune to its own gaze.
If such a monster sees itself in a mirror, it must save versus Petrification or turn itself to stone.
Monsters with petrifying gaze instinctively avoid mirrors and reflective surfaces.
If an attacker surprises such a monster with a mirror, there is a 1-2 on 1d6 chance the monster sees its reflection.

special_attack.name: poison
special_attack.rule: Unless otherwise noted, a character exposed to monster poison must immediately save versus Poison or die.
Neutralize poison can restore a poisoned character if cast within 10 rounds of death.

special_attack.name: swallow_attack
special_attack.rule: Some monsters swallow whole when an unmodified attack throw equals or exceeds a target value stated in the monster description.
A swallowed character suffers the listed damage each round until death or until the monster is killed.
Swallowing may have additional effects stated in the monster's description.
A swallowed character with a sharp weapon may attack from inside with a -4 attack penalty.
If a swallowed character dies and remains in the monster's belly for 6 turns, the body is irrecoverably digested and cannot benefit from restore life and limb.

special_attack.name: trample
special_attack.rule: A trample attack uses the monster's bulk to stomp or crush a target.
Trample gains +4 to the attack throw against human-sized or smaller opponents.
A monster capable of trampling will use trample 3/4 of the time, rolling 1-3 on 1d4, and use other attacks the rest of the time.
Large groups of normal-sized animals, numbering 20 or more, may also trample.
Mass animal trample attacks deal 1d20 damage.

characteristic.name: damage
characteristic.definition: Damage is listed in the same order as attacks.
characteristic.rule: Damage is rolled using the listed die expression as with weapon damage.
Some monsters use weapons.

characteristic.name: save
characteristic.definition: Monsters save as a class and level equivalent.
characteristic.rule: Most monsters save as fighters, but any class progression may be specified.
Unintelligent monsters often save as a fighter of level equal to one-half their Hit Dice, rounded up.

characteristic.name: morale
characteristic.definition: Morale determines whether monsters continue fighting or flee when losing a battle.

procedure.step: Roll 2d6 using the Morale Rolls rule.
Resolve the result using the morale subsystem.

characteristic.rule: Morale scores range from -6 to +4.
A morale of -6 represents a monster that never fights.
A morale of +4 represents a monster that never retreats and never surrenders.
Mindless vermin, constructs, and controlled undead may have morale listed as N/A and never roll morale.

characteristic.name: treasure_type
characteristic.definition: Treasure Type is a letter code from A to R.
characteristic.rule: Treasure Type A yields the smallest hoards and Treasure Type R the largest.
Treasure Type is cross-referenced on the treasure table to determine lair treasure.
Unless otherwise noted, monster treasure is found only in the lair.

characteristic.name: xp
characteristic.definition: Printed experience points are precalculated from Hit Dice and special abilities.
characteristic.rule: If the monster has variable Hit Dice, the printed XP assumes the lowest possible Hit Dice.
XP must be recalculated for more powerful versions with higher Hit Dice.

general_rules.rule: Monster type determines the effectiveness of charm, detection, hold, protection, and sleep spells against the creature.
A creature may belong to more than one monster type.

monster_type.name: animal
monster_type.definition: Real-world creatures of subhuman intelligence, including giant and prehistoric animals.

spell_interactions.rule: Charm animal, speak with animal, and related magic items work only on animals.
Animals are also vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

monster_type.name: construct
monster_type.rule: Skeletons and zombies are undead constructs.

spell_interactions.rule: Constructs count as enchanted creatures for dispel evil and protection from evil.

monster_type.name: enchanted_creature
monster_type.definition: Creatures affected by anti-evil warding and banishment interactions.

spell_interactions.rule: Can be kept at bay by protection from evil.
Can be destroyed or driven off by dispel evil.

membership_rules.rule: All constructs, summoned creatures, and undead are enchanted creatures.
Lycanthropes, shadows, and other fantastic creatures that can only be harmed by magical weapons are also enchanted creatures.

monster_type.name: fantastic_creature
monster_type.definition: Creatures defined by magical powers, impossible body combinations, or both.

spell_interactions.rule: Not affected by charm person or hold person.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

monster_type.name: giant_humanoid
monster_type.definition: Creatures that would be humanoids except for great size and 5 or more Hit Dice.

spell_interactions.rule: Not affected by charm person or hold person.
Vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

monster_type.name: humanoid
monster_type.definition: Creatures no larger than an ogre and possessing 4 or fewer Hit Dice.
monster_type.rule: Humanoids other than humans that have character classes are called demi-humans.
Humans and demi-humans remain humanoids even at 5th level or higher.

spell_interactions.rule: All humanoids are vulnerable to charm person and hold person.

monster_type.name: ooze
monster_type.rule: Different oozes have different immunities and vulnerabilities.

spell_interactions.rule: Can be kept at bay by protection from evil.
Can be destroyed or driven off by dispel evil.
Chaotic summoned creatures are inherently evil for detect evil and protection from evil.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

monster_type.name: undead
monster_type.definition: Creatures that were once alive and now exist as undead horrors.
monster_type.behavior_rule: Most undead do not make a sound when moving.

spell_interactions.rule: All undead are inherently evil for detect evil and protection from evil.
Cannot be affected by spells that affect animals.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.
